texts.li: [fossil,winter] The stream had frozen back from its banks, and in the mud it left {A_nameDef} found a flat stone with a tiny fish in it, every bone in place.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to know how a fish got inside a stone. {B_nameDef} could tell {A_objective}, given an hour.

[coin,summer] {A_nameDef} has been digging holes all summer looking for treasure, and today found some: a small square coin with a hole in the middle, threaded on a rotted string.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to know who carried it. {B_nameDef} has a guess or two.

[skull,!lowtech] {A_nameDef} came back from the scrub with a small skull in a jar, cleaned with a toothbrush that was not {A_possessive} own. {A_nameDef} has named it already, and wants to know what it was.\n\n{B_nameDef} could look it up with {A_objective}.

lines.li: [fossil] {B_nameDef} tells {A_nameDef} about the sea that was here once, and {A_nameDef} wants to know where all the water went, and then where it is now.
[coin] {B_nameDef} thinks the coin is from a trading town that burned long ago. {A_nameDef} has given the town a name, a market and a king since.
[machine] {A_nameDef} has learned from {B_nameDef} that it was part of a radio, and has stopped calling it a brain, mostly.
{A_nameDef} asks {B_nameDef} more questions in an afternoon than the rest of the colony does in a week, and {B_nameDef} answers most of them.
[geode] The stone sits on the windowsill by {A_nameDef}'s bed, where the morning light comes through it purple.
It goes in a box under {A_nameDef}'s bed with {A_possessive} other treasures, and comes out to be looked at whenever anyone asks.
A neighbor's buyer pays {COUNT} silver for it, and their runner brings the silver up to the colony. {A_nameDef} asks twice whether the buyer will look after it.

texts.li: [summer] Water first, then shade: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came for one and stayed for the other, and has spent the whole afternoon looking at {A_nameDef}. At last {X_pronoun} came over and named a price: {COUNT} silver, to forget a face from a notice, from the years when {A_nameDef} was {TALE}.

[colony:Harsh] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} knows what this colony does to people who cross it, and asks {A_nameDef} for silence money anyway, in a low voice and with an eye on the gate. {X_nameDef} remembers {A_nameDef} from {A_possessive} time as {TALE}. The price is {COUNT} silver.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} takes the silver, says {X_pronoun} has a bad memory for faces after all, and is on the road again before anyone can change their mind.
{X_nameDef} is told to say what {X_pronoun} likes, and leaves with nothing but a sour look.

riskLines.li: {X_nameDef} leaves empty-handed and angry, and tells the story at every stop on the way home. {FACTION} know now what {A_nameDef} used to be.

lines.li: Whatever {A_nameDef} says to {X_nameDef}, it is said low and it is said once. {X_nameDef} doesn't mention silver again, and leaves without looking at anyone.

riskLines.li: {A_nameDef} loses {A_possessive} temper halfway through, and {X_nameDef} backs off toward the gate promising that {FACTION} will hear every word.

texts.li: [summer] {FACTION}'s rider came in caked in dust, with a letter for {A_nameDef} from {X_nameDef}, the commander {A_pronoun} served under once. The summer campaign against {ENEMY} has gone on longer than anyone planned, and the wagons are empty.\n\n{X_nameDef} asks for {TALE}, and promises a share of the spoils if they win.

[colony:Generous] "They say your people give," {X_nameDef} writes to {A_nameDef}, {A_possessive} old commander, from {FACTION}'s camp in the field against {ENEMY}. "I hope they say right. We need {TALE}."\n\nIf {FACTION} win, the colony will have a share of the spoils.

lines.li: {FACTION}'s rider takes the supplies off the colony's hands, and a short letter from {A_nameDef} goes with them, signed with {A_possessive} old rank.
{A_nameDef}'s answer wishes {X_nameDef} luck against {ENEMY} and sends nothing else. {A_nameDef} has been short with people since.

texts.li: [doctor,summer] In this heat, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked a long way with a gift on {X_possessive} back, to thank {A_nameDef} for a night years ago when {A_nameDef} kept {X_objective} breathing on a camp table. {X_nameDef} shows the scar to anyone who asks.

[healer,colony:Hospitable] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} heard the colony takes in travelers, and hoped the healer who once set {X_possessive} broken arm might be among them. It's {A_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} has brought a gift, and had to sit down for a moment at the gate.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} sets the gift down in front of {A_nameDef} and tells the story of that night to anyone in earshot, getting the worst parts wrong.
{X_nameDef} says {X_pronoun} owes {A_nameDef} a life anyway, so it might as well be spent here, and asks where the beds are.

riskLines.li: {X_nameDef} can't stay: there are people at home who need {X_objective} the way {X_pronoun} once needed {A_nameDef}. The gift stays with the colony all the same.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} promises to tell the story at every hearth between here and home, and says {X_pronoun} tells it well.

texts.li: [same] {A_nameDef} turned up a sealed crate digging by the wall, and has been turning it over and listening to it ever since. The lock is good work, {A_nameDef} says, and good work can be undone.\n\nA hammer would be quicker. {FACTION} would pay {COUNT} silver for it sealed.

lines.li: {FACTION}'s rider brings {COUNT} silver up to the gate and takes the crate away unopened. The colony will never know what it sold.

texts.li: [fall] The night's storm stripped the last leaves off the old {BEAST} by the colony and then split it with one bolt. Its heartwood is baked dark and hard.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to carve from it. Felled, the rest would be about {COUNT} wood for the winter, or it could stand as it is.

[colony:Artful] Lightning split the old {BEAST} near the colony last night, and {A_nameDef} was out at first light with {A_possessive} hand on the heartwood. A colony that likes beautiful things, {A_nameDef} says, should not burn wood like this.\n\nCut up, it's about {COUNT} wood, or it can be left standing.

lines.li: The tree comes down and most of it is cut up for wood. {A_nameDef} spent the felling looking at the heartwood, and has an idea now that {A_pronoun} sketches on every scrap {A_pronoun} can find.
The split tree comes down in two halves and is cut into {COUNT} wood of seasoned timber, already dry enough to burn.
[winter] The tree is felled and sawn into {COUNT} wood, seasoned on the stump. It will burn hot and slow through the cold nights.
The split tree stays where the sky put it. People have started giving directions by it.

texts.li: [summer] On a hot clear night the sky lit up white and something hit the land {PLACE} hard enough to wake the sleepers. {A_nameDef} found it at sunrise: a pitted black lump in a ring of burnt grass, too hot to touch.\n\nIt's iron, and better iron than any mine gives. {A_nameDef} wants to forge a {TALE} from it.

riskLines.li: {A_nameDef} works the star-iron at the forge, and in the quench it splits along a line nobody could have seen. What comes out of the water is ordinary steel.

lines.li: The fallen star is broken up with picks where it lies, and the pieces wait in the scorched hollow to be hauled in as good steel.
The star stays in its hollow, cooling. In the evenings people walk out to it and put a hand on the black metal.

texts.li: [summer] At sunrise an old {BEAST} came down out of the long grass and stopped just outside the fields, looking at the houses with its head high. It doesn't move when people come near.\n\n{A_nameDef} thinks it means to be followed. It could also be left an offering, or hunted.

[faith:devout] {A_nameDef} saw it first: an old {BEAST} standing at the edge of the colony at dawn, still as a carving, looking at the houses. {A_nameDef} hasn't stopped saying it's a sign.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to follow it when it goes. It could also be left an offering, or hunted.

lines.li: The offering is set down past the fields and left. When someone goes to look, the {BEAST} has gone back into the wild and the food has gone with it.
The hunters are told to take the {BEAST}. A few people at the colony won't look at them while they get ready.
Nobody goes near the {BEAST}. After a while it lowers its head, turns, and goes back into the wild the way it came.

riskLines.li: The smoke doesn't take. The swarm comes out of the hollow like a thrown sack and sees {A_nameDef} all the way back to the houses. The comb stays in the tree, and so do the bees.

lines.li: The map goes back into its old hiding place. Some evenings {A_nameDef} takes it out and looks at the cross, and puts it away again.
